paper.title: No Internal Regret via Neighborhood Watch

settings.name_in_paper: Finite partial-monitoring game, locally observable, non-stochastic opponent
unmapped: Game is locally observable: l_i - l_j in Im S_(i,j)^T for all neighboring actions i,j
Learner knows loss matrix L and signal matrix H
No action completely dominated; best-response cells form a non-degenerate partition
Regret measured as (local) internal regret w.r.t. departure functions phi_{i->j}
settings.definition_quote: Imagine playing a repeated zero-sum game against an opponent (column player) where the loss is defined by a given matrix $L\in \reals^{N\times M}$. ... we (the row player) do not observe the moves of the opponent and instead receive some signal given by the known matrix $H\in \Sigma^{N\times M}$ ... The game is called locally observable if $\ell_i-\ell_j \in \text{Im}~S^\tr_{(i,j)}$ for all neighboring actions $i,j$.

symbols.v_bar: max over neighboring pairs (i,j) of ||v_(i,j)||_inf, where l_j - l_i = S_(i,j)^T v_(i,j)

conditions: no action completely dominated, non-degenerate best-response partition
tuning: gamma = 0 (proof gives additional T N gamma l_bar term)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Local internal regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg} is bounded as \sup_{\phi}\E \left\{ \sum_{t=1}^T (e_{I_t}-e_{\phi(I_t)})^\tr L e_{j_t} \right\} \leq 4N\bar{v}\sqrt{6 (\log N) T} where $\bar{v} = \max_{(i,j)} \|v_{(i,j)}\|_\infty$ and supremum is taken over all local departure functions.

results.notes: Paper's N (number of player actions) mapped to K. Quantity is local internal regret (sup over local departure functions of expected phi-regret); comparator vocabulary has no internal-regret option, best_policy used for departure-function comparator. Proof yields extra TN*gamma*l_bar term; stated bound corresponds to gamma=0. Section 5 claims analysis extends to random signals.

conditions: no action completely dominated, non-degenerate best-response partition

source.quote: Internal regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg} is also bounded as in Theorem~\ref{thm:regret}.

results.notes: Global internal regret (via Lemma 3.1, local internal regret equals internal regret); implies same bound on external regret (best fixed action).
